translations.text: When the judges sat to administer justice, a famine occurred in the land. A man from Bethlehem in the land of Judah went to live as a foreigner in the countryside of Moab, together with his wife and his two sons.

The man's name was Abimelech, and his wife's name was Naomi. His two sons were named Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in the land of Judah. They came to the countryside of Moab and stayed there.
Abimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
They took wives from the land of Moab. One was named Orpah, and the second was named Ruth. They lived there for about ten years.
Both Mahlon and Chilion died. The woman was left a widow, without her husband and without her children.
She and her two daughters-in-law got up and set out to return from the countryside of Moab, because they had heard there that the Lord had visited his people to give them bread.
She left the place where she had been living, with her two daughters-in-law accompanying her. They traveled along the road to return to the land of Judah.
Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you, to her mother's house.
May the Lord show you mercy, just as you have shown mercy to those who died and to me as well. May the Lord reward you, so that each of you finds rest in her husband's house.” Then she kissed them.
They raised their voices and wept, saying, “We will return with you to your people.”
Naomi said to them, “Turn back, my daughters, and go. Why would you come with me? Do I still have sons within me who could become your husbands?
Turn back, my daughters, and go, because I have grown too old to live with another husband. Suppose I said, ‘Do I still have the ability to be with another husband and bear sons?’

Would you stay and wait for them until they grew up? Or would you remain unmarried for their sake, without taking another husband? No, my daughters, do not stay with me, for I am distressed in my heart because of you, because the Lord's hand has gone out against me.”
They raised their voices and wept. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and returned to her people, but Ruth stayed close to her mother-in-law.
Naomi said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and her gods. You too, my daughter, return to your sister-in-law.”

Ruth said to her, “Do not let this force me to leave you behind and go away from you. Wherever you go, I will go with you, and wherever you live, I will stay with you. Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
Wherever you die, I too will die, and they will bury me there. May the Lord do these things to me, and add more besides, for it is death that will separate us from one another.”
When Naomi saw that she was determined to travel with her, she stopped speaking to her about this matter.
The two of them traveled until they came to Bethlehem. When they entered Bethlehem, the news about her spread throughout the whole town, and people said, “This is Naomi!”
She said to them, “Do not call me Naomi. Call me ‘Bitter,’ or ‘The woman who has become bitter,’ because the Almighty, the Powerful One, has made me very bitter.
I went away full, but the Lord brought me back empty. Why would you call me Naomi, when the Lord has humbled me and the Almighty has afflicted me?”
Naomi returned, and with her was Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, who had returned from the countryside of Moab. They came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
Naomi had an acquaintance of her husband's, a powerful man of great strength, from Abimelech's family. His name was Boaz.
Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Let me go out to the field and glean among the heads of grain behind someone in whose eyes I find favor.” Naomi said to her, “Go, my daughter.”
She went and gleaned in the field behind the reapers. She happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from Abimelech's family.
And Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to his reapers, “May the Lord be with you.” They replied, “May the Lord bless you.”
Boaz said to the servant in charge of the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?”
The servant in charge of the reapers answered him, “This is the young Moabite woman who returned with Naomi from the countryside of Moab.
She said, ‘I will go and glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.’ Since she came, she has remained on her feet from morning until evening, without resting at all in the field.”
Boaz said to Ruth, “Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to another person’s field to glean there. Do not leave this place, but stay close to my other young women.

Keep your eyes on the place where they are reaping, and go and follow them. Look, I have ordered the young men not to touch you. When you are thirsty, go to the containers and drink from those the young men fill with water.”
She fell facedown on the ground and bowed, saying to him, “Look, I have found favor with you, so that you take notice of me, even though I am a foreigner.”

Boaz answered her, “I have been fully told about what you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband died, and how you left your father, your mother, and the land where you were born, and went to a people whom you had not known before today. May the Lord repay you for your work.”
And may your reward be complete from the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you have come to seek refuge under his wings.
She said, “My lord, may I find favor with you, because you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your servant. Look, I will be like one of your servants.”

Boaz said to her, “It is already time to eat. Come here and eat some of our bread, and dip your piece in the vinegar.” Ruth sat down beside the reapers, and Boaz prepared food for her to eat. She ate until she was satisfied and kept what was left over.
She got up to glean, and Boaz instructed his servants, saying to them, “Let her gather even among the sheaves, and do not shame her.
Be sure to lift some out for her, and be sure to give her some from the prepared bundles. Let her gather them too, and do not rebuke her.”
She continued gathering in the field until evening. She threshed what she had gathered, and it amounted to a measure of barley.
She picked it up and went into the town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gathered. Ruth brought out what she had left over after eating her fill and gave it to her.

Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where did you gather today, and where did you work? May the man who took notice of you be blessed.” Ruth told her mother-in-law where she had worked, and said to her, “The name of the man who worked with me today is Boaz.”

Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by the Lord, because he has not abandoned his kindness toward the living and the dead.” Naomi also said to her, “The man is closely related to us. He is one of the family who will take us in.”
Ruth said to her mother-in-law, “He also told me, ‘Stay close to my young women until they finish all my harvesting.’”
Naomi said to Ruth, her daughter-in-law, “It is good for you, my daughter, to go with his young women, so that no one seizes you in another field.”
Ruth stayed close to Boaz’s young women, gathering with them until they finished harvesting the barley and the wheat. She lived with her mother-in-law.
Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a place of rest for you, so that things may go well for you?
Now Boaz is our relative, the one whose young women you stayed with. Look, he will be winnowing his barley at the threshing floor tonight.
Wash yourself, anoint yourself, put on your clothes, and go out to the threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
And when he lies down to sleep, notice the place where he will sleep. Then go, uncover his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what you are to do.
Ruth said to her, “I will do everything you tell me.”
And she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.
Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was cheerful. He went to lie down by the heap. Ruth came secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
At midnight the man woke up and was startled. There was a woman lying at his feet!
He said to her, “Who are you?” She said, “I am Ruth, your servant. Spread the edge of your cloak over your servant, because you are a close relative.”
Boaz said to her, “May you be blessed by the Lord, my daughter, because you have shown greater kindness now than before by not pursuing young men, whoever they might be, whether poor or rich.”
“Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do everything you ask, for the whole tribe of the people knows that you are a worthy woman.
And it is true that I am a close relative, but there is a relative closer than I am.

Rest here tonight until daybreak. When morning comes, if that man will take you, that is good; let him take you. But if he is unwilling to take you, I will take you, as the Lord lives. Lie down until morning.”
She lay at his feet until morning, but she got up before one person could recognize another. Boaz said, “Do not let anyone know that a woman came to this threshing floor.”
He said to her, “Bring the wrap you are wearing and hold it.” When she held it, he measured six measures of barley into it and placed them on her. She went into the city.
Ruth went in to her mother-in-law, who said, “Who are you, my daughter?” She said to her, “I am Ruth,” and told her everything the man had done for her.
She also said to her, “He gave me these six measures of barley because he told me, ‘Do not go in to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
She said to her, “Sit down, my daughter, until you know that no word will fail. For the man will not rest until he has finished the matter today.”

Boaz went up to the gate and sat there. Just then the closer relative, the one Boaz had spoken about, was passing by. Boaz said to him, “Come and sit here, you whose name is hidden or unknown.” He came and sat down.
Boaz took ten men from among the elders of the city and said to them, “Sit here.” And they sat down.
Boaz said to the close relative, “About the portion of land belonging to our brother Abimelech, which was given to Naomi, who returned from the country of Moab:

I myself said that I would bring the matter to your attention, saying, ‘Acquire the portion for yourself in the presence of those sitting here and in the presence of the elders of the people.’ If you will claim your right to it, take it. But if you will not take it, tell me so that I may know, because there is no one besides you to take it, and I come after you.” He said, “I will take it.”

Boaz said to him, “On the day you acquire the field from Naomi and from Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the man who died, you will also acquire Ruth herself [?], so as to preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance.”
The close relative said, “I cannot take it for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. Take it for yourself in my place, because I cannot take it.”

And this was the custom from earliest times in Israel concerning redemption by a relative and exchange, to confirm every matter: a man took off his sandal and gave it to his neighbor. This was the testimony in Israel.
The close relative said to Boaz, “Take it for yourself in my place.” He removed his sandal and gave it to him.
Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I have acquired from Naomi everything belonging to Abimelech and everything belonging to Chilion and Mahlon.

And I have taken Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s wife, as my wife, to preserve the dead man’s name on his inheritance, so that the dead man’s name will not be erased from among his brothers or from the tribe of his people. You are witnesses today.”

And all the people at the gate said, “We are witnesses.” And the elders said, “May the Lord make your wife, who is coming into your house, like Rachel and Leah, who together built the house of Israel. May she achieve success in Ephrathah, and may a name be established in Bethlehem.”
"And may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring that the Lord will give you by this young woman."
Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He had intercourse with her, and the Lord enabled her to give birth, and she bore a son.
And the women said to Naomi, “Blessed is the Lord, who has not left you today without a close family redeemer, so that your name may be proclaimed in Israel.”
"And he will restore your life and sustain your [?], because your daughter-in-law, who loves you, has borne him to you. She is better to you than seven sons."
And Naomi took the little child, placed him in her lap, and became his nurse.
And her neighbors said, "A son has been born to Naomi." And they named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
And these are the descendants of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron.
And Hezron fathered Aram, and Aram fathered Amminadab.
And Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.
And Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed.
And Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.
